title: Elevated-Temperature Tribo-Corrosion Response of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: A eutectic high-entropy alloy, likely of the AlCoCrFeNi or AlCoCrFeNi2.1 type, exhibiting a fine lamellar FCC + B2/BCC microstructure.
recollection.intervention: Reciprocating or pin-on-disk tribo-corrosion testing carried out in a high-temperature electrochemical cell, probably between room temperature and 600–800 °C, with concurrent electrochemical monitoring (e.g., open-circuit potential and potentiodynamic polarization).
recollection.structure: The pre-existing lamellar eutectic decomposes near the surface during sliding; high-temperature oxidation forms a mixed Cr/Al-rich spinel or alumina/glass-like glaze layer that gradually smooths the wear track.
recollection.mechanism: Wear, corrosion, and oxidation act synergistically. At intermediate temperatures the oxide scale is mechanically disrupted, giving maximum material loss; at higher temperatures a continuous, adherent oxide glaze forms that suppresses both corrosion current and wear rate.
recollection.results: Total material loss (synergy factor) increases from ~1 × 10⁻³ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ at room temperature to ~3 × 10⁻³ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ at 400 °C, then drops to ~0.5 × 10⁻³ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ at 700 °C due to formation of a protective tribo-oxide. Corrosion current density peaks at ~1 mA cm⁻² at 400 °C and falls to <0.1 mA cm⁻² at 700 °C. Overall, the alloy shows competitive or superior high-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with conventional Ni-based superalloys.

score.note: The recollection partially identifies reciprocating tribo-corrosion with electrochemical monitoring and a fine lamellar FCC/L12–B2-type structure, but misses the thermal-shock comparison, DS2205 comparator, actual 25–100 °C range, and test parameters. Its claimed surface decomposition and protective high-temperature glaze conflict with the retained lamellar structure and unstable, repeatedly ruptured tribo-layer at 100 °C. The temperature-dependent mechanism and all reported numerical trends/values are incorrect.
